claims.statement: deepagents-code (dcode) is a prebuilt terminal coding agent that packages the deepagents SDK harness together with a terminal experience, persistence, tools, skills, and optional sandboxed execution, as a reference implementation.

dcode has two runtime halves that run in separate processes: a terminal client that owns presentation and input (interactive or headless output plus approvals), and an agent server that owns the agent runtime and connects the model, tools, memory, skills, and backend.
A process-wide sandbox is reserved by the first workspace that claims it, and incompatible LangSmith tracing/redaction settings also prevent workspace sharing in the same server process.

Tool-free auxiliary model preparation deep-copies request defaults while removing tool, function, parallel-tool-call, and MCP-server settings, including nested provider option containers; the resulting model copy retains provider HTTP clients.

Thread-title generation creates a tool-free chat request from bounded non-hidden human and assistant conversation text, disables callbacks, records the owning thread in metadata, and normalizes the result to the manual-name safety rules.

The app binds detached thread-name generation to a thread and environment-mutation lock, charges it through side-question accounting, refreshes its side cost, and only auto-saves an absent name after the first completed response.

Remote offload cancellation sends the operation-specific cancel request and does not propagate caller cancellation until the server acknowledges a `cancelled` or `finished` terminal status; the wait is bounded to ten seconds.

`TerminalTitle` accepts only plain documented fields in its template, sanitizes and bounds emitted titles, pushes/pops the terminal title stack only around a successfully started TTY stream, and treats title rendering or writes as cosmetic failures.

The TUI serializes out-of-run goal/rubric mutations with graph checkpoint activity, waits for agent quiescence, and persists TUI-owned goal state through the local or remote graph; paused or complete goals withhold the public rubric while retaining the sticky rubric for restoration.

Goal/rubric model context is a schema-versioned, fingerprinted `HumanMessage` marked `goal_state`; it is explicitly classified as internal so user-facing transcript and derived-conversation paths must hide it.

Before a normal model call, the app ensures a visible valid goal-state notice with the desired fingerprint, defers a replacement when effective conversation history has unanswered tool calls, and refuses to send the turn if goal/rubric persistence fails.

Goal notice rendering projects actionability from persisted channels, escapes and tags embedded objective/criteria/status text, fails closed by suppressing oversized content with do-not-work guidance, and treats an unrecognized stored status as paused.

A skill invocation sends only a normalized skill name, optional arguments, and pinned-skill metadata to the server; the client renders a pending row and fills it only when a separate pinned instruction message returns, while an unreadable, oversized, or instruction-less skill body fails invocation.

Skill discovery merges built-in, plugin, user, project, agent-alias, and experimental Claude roots in increasing precedence, and skill content loading resolves paths then rejects targets outside the pre-resolved allowed roots.

External skill-directory approvals are stored as the canonical directory shown to the user; the trust enforcement path re-verifies entries against symlink swaps, and corrupt or unrecognized trust storage fails closed to no trusted directories.

Classifier-backed Auto mode requires exact one-to-one classifier decisions for reviewed tool calls, supports a per-run classifier model override, and validates construction/inference timeout budgets as positive finite values.

Auto classifier failures fail closed: unavailable or malformed review does not approve calls, repeated unavailable/denial conditions route to human fallback, a repeated configured-model construction fault is latched until successful review, and a failed counter write requires human approval.

Auto approval emits opaque started/completed lifecycle events, and the Textual adapter accepts them only from the main agent with an exact validated shape; it pauses reviewed rows during review and recovers a malformed completion so rows do not remain frozen.
The Textual adapter hides nested Auto classifier stream chunks from the conversation transcript by recognizing the `auto_mode_classifier` stream source.
dcode 0.1.85 is the package release declared consistently by its runtime version module and project metadata.

Approval mode is a validated per-thread live record whose key is a SHA-256 digest of the thread ID; invalid, unavailable, or unreadable store records fail closed to Manual, while the interactive cycle conditionally offers Auto and YOLO.

Before first interactive enable, Auto requires explicit Enter confirmation and YOLO requires explicit acknowledgement; cancellation does not persist their local records or activate the requested mode, and YOLO's Manual choice changes to Manual instead.

Auto's first-enable notice discloses the classifier review model as either the code-writing model or a separate one, escapes its model label for Markdown, and routes notice links through the shared checked URL opener rather than Textual's automatic link handling.

Auto and YOLO first-enable state shares an install-local, versioned `approval.json`; updates are serialized across threads and processes, atomically written with private permissions, merge the two records, and treat missing, stale, or corrupt data as unacknowledged.

dcode constrains Textual to versions 8.2.8 through before 9 because UI patches and custom rendering depend on upstream behavior and private wrapping/compositor offset contracts; message pointer hit testing specifically relies on the private `offset` style metadata.
